2	
3	This bounded renderer loads the existing `src/robot.ts` controller, calls
4	`spriteFor` for south/east/north/west, and paints the actual destination PNGs at
5	1x and 3x nearest sampling on `#172336`. These scales and background are observation
6	conditions. They do not add an owner-approved palette or presentation requirement.
7	The original planning example stays unchanged; a production evaluation must supply
8	its own explicit assignment before generating the missing directions.
9	
10	Run with Node supporting `node:module.stripTypeScriptTypes` and a locally installed
11	Chrome or Edge. No browser configuration or profile is shared with the user.
12	The checker uses the existing Python/Pillow environment.
13	
14	```powershell
15	node examples/delegation/renderer/capture.mjs --project C:/ABS/CONSUMER --out C:/ABS/CONSUMER/work/robot-capture-01
16	.venv/Scripts/python.exe examples/delegation/renderer/check.py --project C:/ABS/CONSUMER --capture C:/ABS/CONSUMER/work/robot-capture-01 --out C:/ABS/CONSUMER/work/robot-check-01.json
17	```
18	
19	An explicit `--browser C:/ABS/chrome.exe` may be supplied to capture. The output
20	directory and checker output must be new. Failures preserve their receipts; use a
21	new path after correction. For interactive inspection, run
22	`node examples/delegation/renderer/server.mjs --project C:/ABS/CONSUMER` and open
23	the printed loopback URL, then stop that server when finished.
24	
25	Required inputs are `src/robot.ts`, `assets/robot-base.png`, and
26	`assets/robot/{south,east,north,west}.png`. The south file must preserve the exact
27	base bytes. Each directional output must be a visible transparent 32x32 RGBA PNG.
28	The actual controller export and `spriteFor` must map every direction to its
29	matching filename. Missing files, mapping changes, nontransparent images, wrong
30	dimensions, changed inputs, altered capture files, and mismatched screenshot
31	pixels fail the mechanical check.

# Directional robot consumer observation

This bounded renderer loads the existing `src/robot.ts` controller, calls
`spriteFor` for south/east/north/west, and paints the actual destination PNGs at
1x and 3x nearest sampling on `#172336`. These scales and background are observation
conditions. They do not add an owner-approved palette or presentation requirement.
The original planning example stays unchanged; a production evaluation must supply
its own explicit assignment before generating the missing directions.

Run with Node supporting `node:module.stripTypeScriptTypes` and a locally installed
Chrome or Edge. No browser configuration or profile is shared with the user.
The checker uses the existing Python/Pillow environment.

```powershell
node examples/delegation/renderer/capture.mjs --project C:/ABS/CONSUMER --out C:/ABS/CONSUMER/work/robot-capture-01
.venv/Scripts/python.exe examples/delegation/renderer/check.py --project C:/ABS/CONSUMER --capture C:/ABS/CONSUMER/work/robot-capture-01 --out C:/ABS/CONSUMER/work/robot-check-01.json
```

An explicit `--browser C:/ABS/chrome.exe` may be supplied to capture. The output
directory and checker output must be new. Failures preserve their receipts; use a
new path after correction. For interactive inspection, run
`node examples/delegation/renderer/server.mjs --project C:/ABS/CONSUMER` and open
the printed loopback URL, then stop that server when finished.

Required inputs are `src/robot.ts`, `assets/robot-base.png`, and
`assets/robot/{south,east,north,west}.png`. The south file must preserve the exact
base bytes. Each directional output must be a visible transparent 32x32 RGBA PNG.
The actual controller export and `spriteFor` must map every direction to its
matching filename. Missing files, mapping changes, nontransparent images, wrong
dimensions, changed inputs, altered capture files, and mismatched screenshot
pixels fail the mechanical check.

`capture.json` retains observed mappings, source/output hashes, browser identity,
scaled canvas images and their screenshot positions. `inputs.json` binds the
pre-capture inputs and renderer sources; `execution.json` records completion and
owned browser/server/profile cleanup. The checker compares decoded source pixels,
alpha compositing, nearest scaling and screenshot crops independently with Pillow.

The report does **not** decide whether a direction looks correct, whether all views
preserve the robot's identity/volume, or whether the artwork is suitable. Inspect
the source and delivered images plus `destination.png`, then record the visual
review separately. Copying one sprite to every direction can pass the mechanical
checks and still fail that review. The synthetic test fixture does exactly that
to test rendering without claiming new art or directional acceptance.

This supports the existing example controller. It is not a new generic
`consumer-execute` profile or qualification of a separate game engine.

Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.
43	
44	Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.
45

Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.
47

Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.

The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.

Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. `pixl_commit` accepts a JSON `document` directly or a `candidate` wire-file path; both use the same validation. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Specialist → caller at completion
72	
73	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
74	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
75	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
76	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
77	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
78	
79	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
80	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
81	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
82	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
83	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
84	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
85	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
86	
87	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
88	
89	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
90	
91	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
92	
93	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
94	
95	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
96	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
97	`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The

# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
changing the user's global configuration.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
without manufacturing PLAR or production records:

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
not automatically summarized.

For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:

```json
{
  "status": "partial",
  "caller": {
    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
    "integration": {
      "status": "not_performed",
      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
    },
    "issues": [
      {
        "category": "unfinished_work",
        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.

Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

1	# Request and criteria handoff
2	
3	Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.
4	
5	## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract
6	
7	Use the focused authoring context described in [family delivery](family-delivery.md)
8	to locate current records before exploring histories. Keep a proposal's shared
9	source index once and reference its entries from individual clauses; preserve each
10	clause's authority, scope and exact locator. Do not duplicate whole reports in
11	every criterion, abbreviate literal checks into a group summary, or treat the
12	index's source class as requirement authority. Read the original source text for
13	the comparison; retrieve a complete record/history only where it bears on the
14	decision. Exact connected review remains the handoff for adoption.
15	
16	For a connected family/stage plan, use the adapter's returned `request_review`
17	arguments and retain that exact report as described in
18	[the connected handoff](#connected-family-and-stage-handoff). It supplies the saved
19	criteria and request evidence without manually rebuilding a candidate packet.
20	
21	For other contracts, save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:
22	
23	- `version`: 1.
24	- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
25	- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
26	- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
27	- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
28	- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.
29	
30	Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.
31	
32	Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.
33	
34	Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.
35	
36	### Measured facts in creative requests
37	
38	Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.
39	
40	Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
41	`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
42	`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
43	A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
44	same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
45	are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.
46	
47	The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.
48	
49	## Resolve source evidence for the comparison
50	
51	For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
52	with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
53	--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
54	with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
55	invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
56	the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.
57	
58	Copy a host-spilled tool report as exact bytes before inspecting or formatting it.
59	These tool reports are UTF-8 JSON: use an explicit UTF-8 decoder (for example,
60	`Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`), not the Windows process default. If saving a
61	formatted copy, compare its parsed value with the raw report before returning its
62	path/hash. A new file hash alone cannot detect text changed by a wrong decoder.
63	Keep the raw report alongside any formatted copy.
64	
65	When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
66	`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
67	reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.
68	
69	Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
70	`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
71	saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
72	locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
73	for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
74	mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.
75	
76	The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
77	labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
78	not an automatic grant of owner authority.
79	
80	## Caller: inspect before adopting
81	
82	### Connected family and stage handoff
83	
84	`pixl_production_plan` and `pixl_stage_prepare` return `request_review` arguments
85	for this same review tool. Pass that object to `pixl_request_review`; `packet`
86	names the store's `state.px`, `plan` names its exact connected-plan X, and `job`
87	is present after preparation. Existing plans can use those IDs directly. The
88	report includes every authored member and collective criterion with its full Q
89	ID, record hash, literal check and source evidence. Authority starts unclassified:
90	source presence or a validator pass cannot assign it. Changed plan/source/PLAR
91	identities remain visible so historical interpretation can be reviewed without
92	making an obsolete request current.
93	
94	The specialist returns this report's path/hash, explicit choices and any proposed
95	corrections. The caller reads the original evidence and records one
96	`criterion_comparisons` entry for **each** returned ID, including collective rules:
97	
98	```json
99	{
100	  "review_scope_sha256": "REPORT_REVIEW_SCOPE_HASH",
101	  "criterion_comparisons": [{
102	    "criterion": "EXACT_Q_ID",
103	    "record_sha256": "Q_RECORD_HASH",
104	    "source_obligation": "What the cited source actually requires, with locator",
105	    "authority_basis": "Required outcome, scoped expert choice, observation, or mixed clauses",
106	    "scope": "The asset, stage or chosen construction this rule applies to",
107	    "literal_delta": "What the exact rule adds, drops or leaves unchanged",
108	    "discriminating_alternative": "A concrete alternative that tests that difference",
109	    "disposition": "Keep, clarify or correct, with the proposed artifact identity"
110	  }]
111	}
112	```
113	
114	Split mixed-authority clauses in these explanations. A sound construction does
115	not make every clause an owner requirement; nor does an expert choice need to be
116	removed merely because other valid methods exist. Keep the required artistic
117	outcome and identify the chosen method's narrower scope. Do not substitute one
118	grouped style/geometry assertion for this comparison.
119	
120	Call the same tool with `comparison` pointing to the saved caller file to check
121	coverage and identity. Missing, repeated, stale or incomplete rows are reported.
122	`complete:true` means structural coverage only; semantic judgment remains the
123	caller’s responsibility, and `consistent` stays null in the tool report. Record
124	the caller's own disposition separately. Save a corrected proposal beside the
125	old plan/request when necessary; do not rewrite historical criteria, transplant
126	acceptance or prepare another job merely to repair the review.
127	
128	### Compare the original sources and exact contract
129	
130	For either route, open the retained packet/report and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:
131	
132	1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
133	2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
134	3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
135	4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
136	5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.
137	
138	For each rejection criterion, save one concise comparison using the following
139	sequence. A table or JSON is sufficient; this is the caller's actual reasoning about
140	the source, not a worksheet to have the specialist certify for itself.
141	
142	1. **Source obligation.** Derive the minimum required outcome from the original source
143	   wording and locator before using the draft criterion as its paraphrase. State what
144	   the source leaves open. For an expert criterion, identify the actual expert choice
145	   and candidate scope instead of inventing owner authority.
146	2. **Literal condition and additions.** Compare the entire check with that obligation.
147	   Identify the exact added or omitted words/clauses, including extent, composition,
148	   exclusions, comparisons and numerical bounds. A supported noun does not establish
149	   support for its modifiers. Read the check itself, not just its basis or label.
150	3. **Discriminating alternative.** For each added restriction, describe a plausible
151	   asset that keeps the source obligation true while making that specific restriction
152	   false. Name the clause being tested and whether the literal check would reject it.
153	   Merely changing a value the check already permits does not test that restriction.
154	   If the source itself excludes the alternative, identify the exact source support.
155	4. **Disposition.** Keep the required outcome; remove an unsupported narrowing from
156	   that rule or split it into an explicitly scoped expert choice with its own rationale.
157	   An ambiguous condition that could reject a valid alternative needs clearer wording;
158	   do not approve it by silently giving it a more permissive interpretation. Verify the
159	   correction in the returned artifact before marking the contract consistent.
160	
161	For example, a requirement for a readable silhouette does not itself require an
162	outlined silhouette. Comparing two outline colours leaves the added outline rule
163	untested; a readable outline-free construction tests it. The specialist may still
164	recommend an outline for this sample and explain its artistic value. The comparison
165	preserves that expertise while accurately describing who chose it and what it binds.
166	
167	Cover every rejection rule; group only genuinely identical ones. Retain the source
168	quote/bounds, literal delta, tested alternative and disposition together. A general
169	"the brief permits flexibility" statement or a prompt-choice label elsewhere cannot
170	cancel a restriction still present in an owner-authority acceptance condition.
171	
172	Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
173	establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
174	shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
175	reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
176	criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
177	to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
178	candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
179	condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
180	correction must still specify the route its future acceptance will actually need.
181	Do not call a corrected contract operable merely because its source locators resolve.
182	
183	When reviewing a specialist's response to a discrepancy, re-open the literal check.
184	An added attribution or a claim that a conventional construction excludes no valid
185	alternatives does not remove an unchanged mandatory recipe. Retain the source's
186	qualitative outcome as required and place the expert construction in a scoped proposal;
187	judge actual recognizability without declaring one geometric recipe universal.
188	
189	Resolve every evidence-report diagnostic before calling a locator verified. For a

# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Use the focused authoring context described in [family delivery](family-delivery.md)
to locate current records before exploring histories. Keep a proposal's shared
source index once and reference its entries from individual clauses; preserve each
clause's authority, scope and exact locator. Do not duplicate whole reports in
every criterion, abbreviate literal checks into a group summary, or treat the
index's source class as requirement authority. Read the original source text for
the comparison; retrieve a complete record/history only where it bears on the
decision. Exact connected review remains the handoff for adoption.

For a connected family/stage plan, use the adapter's returned `request_review`
arguments and retain that exact report as described in
[the connected handoff](#connected-family-and-stage-handoff). It supplies the saved
criteria and request evidence without manually rebuilding a candidate packet.

For other contracts, save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

## Resolve source evidence for the comparison

For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.

Copy a host-spilled tool report as exact bytes before inspecting or formatting it.
These tool reports are UTF-8 JSON: use an explicit UTF-8 decoder (for example,
`Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`), not the Windows process default. If saving a
formatted copy, compare its parsed value with the raw report before returning its
path/hash. A new file hash alone cannot detect text changed by a wrong decoder.
Keep the raw report alongside any formatted copy.

When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.

Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.

The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
not an automatic grant of owner authority.

### Connected family and stage handoff

`pixl_production_plan` and `pixl_stage_prepare` return `request_review` arguments
for this same review tool. Pass that object to `pixl_request_review`; `packet`

source presence or a validator pass cannot assign it. Changed plan/source/PLAR

making an obsolete request current.

The specialist returns this report's path/hash, explicit choices and any proposed
corrections. The caller reads the original evidence and records one

```json
{
  "review_scope_sha256": "REPORT_REVIEW_SCOPE_HASH",
  "criterion_comparisons": [{
    "criterion": "EXACT_Q_ID",
    "record_sha256": "Q_RECORD_HASH",
    "source_obligation": "What the cited source actually requires, with locator",
    "authority_basis": "Required outcome, scoped expert choice, observation, or mixed clauses",
    "scope": "The asset, stage or chosen construction this rule applies to",
    "literal_delta": "What the exact rule adds, drops or leaves unchanged",
    "discriminating_alternative": "A concrete alternative that tests that difference",
    "disposition": "Keep, clarify or correct, with the proposed artifact identity"
  }]
}
```

Split mixed-authority clauses in these explanations. A sound construction does
not make every clause an owner requirement; nor does an expert choice need to be
removed merely because other valid methods exist. Keep the required artistic
outcome and identify the chosen method's narrower scope. Do not substitute one
grouped style/geometry assertion for this comparison.

Call the same tool with `comparison` pointing to the saved caller file to check
coverage and identity. Missing, repeated, stale or incomplete rows are reported.
`complete:true` means structural coverage only; semantic judgment remains the
caller’s responsibility, and `consistent` stays null in the tool report. Record
the caller's own disposition separately. Save a corrected proposal beside the
old plan/request when necessary; do not rewrite historical criteria, transplant
acceptance or prepare another job merely to repair the review.

### Compare the original sources and exact contract

For either route, open the retained packet/report and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:

1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.

For each rejection criterion, save one concise comparison using the following
sequence. A table or JSON is sufficient; this is the caller's actual reasoning about
the source, not a worksheet to have the specialist certify for itself.

1. **Source obligation.** Derive the minimum required outcome from the original source
   wording and locator before using the draft criterion as its paraphrase. State what
   the source leaves open. For an expert criterion, identify the actual expert choice
   and candidate scope instead of inventing owner authority.
2. **Literal condition and additions.** Compare the entire check with that obligation.
   Identify the exact added or omitted words/clauses, including extent, composition,
   exclusions, comparisons and numerical bounds. A supported noun does not establish
   support for its modifiers. Read the check itself, not just its basis or label.
3. **Discriminating alternative.** For each added restriction, describe a plausible
   asset that keeps the source obligation true while making that specific restriction
   false. Name the clause being tested and whether the literal check would reject it.
   Merely changing a value the check already permits does not test that restriction.
   If the source itself excludes the alternative, identify the exact source support.
4. **Disposition.** Keep the required outcome; remove an unsupported narrowing from
   that rule or split it into an explicitly scoped expert choice with its own rationale.
   An ambiguous condition that could reject a valid alternative needs clearer wording;
   do not approve it by silently giving it a more permissive interpretation. Verify the
   correction in the returned artifact before marking the contract consistent.

For example, a requirement for a readable silhouette does not itself require an
outlined silhouette. Comparing two outline colours leaves the added outline rule
untested; a readable outline-free construction tests it. The specialist may still
recommend an outline for this sample and explain its artistic value. The comparison
preserves that expertise while accurately describing who chose it and what it binds.

Cover every rejection rule; group only genuinely identical ones. Retain the source
quote/bounds, literal delta, tested alternative and disposition together. A general
"the brief permits flexibility" statement or a prompt-choice label elsewhere cannot
cancel a restriction still present in an owner-authority acceptance condition.

Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
correction must still specify the route its future acceptance will actually need.
Do not call a corrected contract operable merely because its source locators resolve.

When reviewing a specialist's response to a discrepancy, re-open the literal check.
An added attribution or a claim that a conventional construction excludes no valid
alternatives does not remove an unchanged mandatory recipe. Retain the source's
qualitative outcome as required and place the expert construction in a scoped proposal;
judge actual recognizability without declaring one geometric recipe universal.

Resolve every evidence-report diagnostic before calling a locator verified. For a
text citation, open the actual source, use its file-local inclusive bounds and save
those bounds in the corrected packet; a nearby matching sentence does not repair a
wrong range. An unresolved named or visual reference needs actual inspection and a
recorded finding. A source hash alone never verifies the cited location or its meaning.

The [delegation boundary](delegation.md#caller--specialist) distinguishes unchanged
historical evidence from the editable corrected proposal. A caller must not freeze

against the source. Use the profile's visual-role distinctions when translating colour,

Do not create another provider job merely to correct documentation, transplant old

Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.

If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.

If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.

## Carry the comparison through production

Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.

The final caller opens the delivered assets, checks the actual request and output against this contract, and records its own observations. Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. For a rejected candidate, retain the failure and the revised request/criteria; changing a checker merely to pass the candidate is a contract change, not an asset correction.

When an artistic explanation asserts a measurement, compare that assertion with
its actual data and coordinate convention. Reproducing a bounding box does not

should remain approximate. Correct an inconsistent explanation in a new observation

2

4	`view: "caller"` saves the existing immutable version-1 handoff, then returns a
5	bounded presentation of that same captured selection. The default `view: "receipt"`
6	and saved bytes for identical inputs are unchanged. There is no new ledger, UDL
7	record, provider action or acceptance event.
8	
9	## Agent-authored compact fields
10	
11	`details.status` retains its existing assignment meaning: `delivered`, `partial`,
12	`needs_input` or `blocked`. It does not follow automatically from production state.
13	An optional `details.caller` object supplies the following closed fields:
14	
15	| Field | Content |
16	| --- | --- |
17	| `summary` | Nonempty text, at most 600 characters |
18	| `artifacts` | At most 12 actual project file references |
19	| `reports` | At most 12 references to separately retained detailed reports |
20	| `issues` | At most 12 objects with `category`, `summary` and optional `recovery` |
21	| `integration` | An agent observation with `status`, `summary` and optional `evidence` file references |
22	
23	All fields are optional. Omission means not reported, not a pass or an unavailable
24	check. An absent caller block is returned as `caller.present: false`; arbitrary
25	legacy details are never heuristically summarized. Existing receipt mode does not
26	reinterpret a legacy field called `caller`.
27	
28	File references contain exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`. Paths are nonempty
29	forward-slash project-relative paths, at most 512 characters. SHA-256 is 64 lowercase
30	hexadecimal digits; role is nonempty text of at most 96 characters. The operation
31	confines and hashes every declared artifact, report and integration-evidence file
32	before publishing. It does not copy those files or guarantee that they remain
33	unchanged after that observation. Roles and judgments are supplied by the agent.
34	
35	Issue categories are `invalid_authoring`, `stale_local_state`, `missing_capability`,
36	`uncertain_remote_result`, `unavailable_observation` and `unfinished_work`.
37	Summary and recovery text each have the same 600-character bound. The category is
38	an agent's classification, not an automatic diagnosis or authorization to retry.
39	
40	Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
41	`not_in_scope`. Its summary is required and bounded to 600 characters; evidence
42	uses the same file-reference array. The report labels this block `agent_authored`.
43	A claimed integration pass does not establish a stored verdict or artistic acceptance.
44	
45	The complete caller block must encode to at most 8192 bytes as finite UTF-8 JSON
46	with compact separators. Oversized or malformed blocks, unreadable files and
47	hash mismatches fail before a new handoff is published. Detailed observations
48	belong in linked files or the existing unrestricted expert details, not truncated
49	inside the compact block. `pixl.caller_result.CALLER_SCHEMA` describes the shape.
50	
51	## Returned facts and exact retrieval
52	
53	Caller view retains every default receipt field (`path`, `sha256`, `asset_id`,
54	`requirements_hash`, `state_hash`, `next`, `scope`) and adds:
55	
56	- `assignment`: the supplied status and its `agent_authored` basis.
57	- `caller`: presence, authored fields and the file-verification observation.
58	- `production`: captured task ID/state, selection currency, criterion counts for
59	  current nominees, job counts and delivery facts. Unperformed/unavailable checks
60	  remain unresolved. Counts never imply every operation or visual check succeeded.
61	- `store`: the exact continuation's project-relative production store.
62	- `details_ref` and `resume_ref`: immutable file path/hash, physical line range,
63	  UTF-8 byte count and JSON pointer for the saved section.
64	- `resume_inline`, `resume_bytes`, and the unchanged `resume` when it occupies at
65	  most 4096 compact UTF-8 JSON bytes. Larger continuations are omitted as a whole
66	  and remain retrievable through `resume_ref`; there is no partial rewritten resume.
67	- `refresh`: the exact focused `pixl_plar_read` operation and arguments. Reread
68	  after state or source changes and compare requirements/state identities before
69	  acting. This operation is a read instruction, not automatic execution.
70	
71	Delivery remains exactly the existing handoff's derived delivery value. If larger
72	than 2048 compact JSON bytes, `production.delivery_inline` is false and
73	`delivery_ref` identifies `/resume/delivery`; the containing resume line range is
74	returned intact. `delivery_complete` and `delivery_observed` remain visible.
75	Destination bytes and declared family criteria do not establish undeclared engine
76	or artistic checks. Assignment status remains independent even when delivery is
77	complete or an external destination subsequently changes without a state revision.
78	
79	Use existing `source` / `pixl_source` with the locator's path, SHA-256, line bounds
80	and an adequate byte budget. The field slice is exact JSON source text and can
81	include its trailing object-member comma. The JSON pointer identifies its meaning;
82	no new reader tool is required. A larger section may be read in smaller physical
83	line ranges under the same file hash. When parsing as an object, open the complete
84	immutable file or wrap the returned member after removing its trailing comma.
85	
86	Caller-view errors use `caller_result_input`, `caller_result_size`,
87	`caller_artifact_unavailable` and `caller_artifact_stale`; existing `path_escape`,
88	`handoff_stale`, `handoff_state` and `handoff_corrupt` retain their meaning. A file
89	failure identifies the declared file's `path` and `expected_file_sha256`; a hash
90	mismatch also returns `observed_file_sha256`. Its allocation `plar_path` stays
91	separate from that artifact path in structured diagnostics. A file
92	export failure does not undo an already saved handoff. Reconcile its returned
93	operation result before repeating the save; never treat it as a reason to repeat
94	remote generation.

check. An absent caller block is returned as `caller.present: false`; arbitrary
legacy details are never heuristically summarized. Existing receipt mode does not
reinterpret a legacy field called `caller`.

File references contain exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`. Paths are nonempty
forward-slash project-relative paths, at most 512 characters. SHA-256 is 64 lowercase
hexadecimal digits; role is nonempty text of at most 96 characters. The operation
confines and hashes every declared artifact, report and integration-evidence file
before publishing. It does not copy those files or guarantee that they remain
unchanged after that observation. Roles and judgments are supplied by the agent.

Issue categories are `invalid_authoring`, `stale_local_state`, `missing_capability`,
`uncertain_remote_result`, `unavailable_observation` and `unfinished_work`.
Summary and recovery text each have the same 600-character bound. The category is
an agent's classification, not an automatic diagnosis or authorization to retry.

Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
`not_in_scope`. Its summary is required and bounded to 600 characters; evidence
uses the same file-reference array. The report labels this block `agent_authored`.
A claimed integration pass does not establish a stored verdict or artistic acceptance.

The complete caller block must encode to at most 8192 bytes as finite UTF-8 JSON
with compact separators. Oversized or malformed blocks, unreadable files and
hash mismatches fail before a new handoff is published. Detailed observations
belong in linked files or the existing unrestricted expert details, not truncated
inside the compact block. `pixl.caller_result.CALLER_SCHEMA` describes the shape.

## Returned facts and exact retrieval

Caller view retains every default receipt field (`path`, `sha256`, `asset_id`,
`requirements_hash`, `state_hash`, `next`, `scope`) and adds:

- `assignment`: the supplied status and its `agent_authored` basis.
- `caller`: presence, authored fields and the file-verification observation.
- `production`: captured task ID/state, selection currency, criterion counts for
  current nominees, job counts and delivery facts. Unperformed/unavailable checks
  remain unresolved. Counts never imply every operation or visual check succeeded.
- `store`: the exact continuation's project-relative production store.
- `details_ref` and `resume_ref`: immutable file path/hash, physical line range,
  UTF-8 byte count and JSON pointer for the saved section.
- `resume_inline`, `resume_bytes`, and the unchanged `resume` when it occupies at
  most 4096 compact UTF-8 JSON bytes. Larger continuations are omitted as a whole
  and remain retrievable through `resume_ref`; there is no partial rewritten resume.
- `refresh`: the exact focused `pixl_plar_read` operation and arguments. Reread
  after state or source changes and compare requirements/state identities before
  acting. This operation is a read instruction, not automatic execution.

Delivery remains exactly the existing handoff's derived delivery value. If larger
than 2048 compact JSON bytes, `production.delivery_inline` is false and
`delivery_ref` identifies `/resume/delivery`; the containing resume line range is
returned intact. `delivery_complete` and `delivery_observed` remain visible.
Destination bytes and declared family criteria do not establish undeclared engine
or artistic checks. Assignment status remains independent even when delivery is
complete or an external destination subsequently changes without a state revision.

Use existing `source` / `pixl_source` with the locator's path, SHA-256, line bounds
and an adequate byte budget. The field slice is exact JSON source text and can
include its trailing object-member comma. The JSON pointer identifies its meaning;
no new reader tool is required. A larger section may be read in smaller physical
line ranges under the same file hash. When parsing as an object, open the complete
immutable file or wrap the returned member after removing its trailing comma.

Caller-view errors use `caller_result_input`, `caller_result_size`,
`caller_artifact_unavailable` and `caller_artifact_stale`; existing `path_escape`,
`handoff_stale`, `handoff_state` and `handoff_corrupt` retain their meaning. A file
failure identifies the declared file's `path` and `expected_file_sha256`; a hash
mismatch also returns `observed_file_sha256`. Its allocation `plar_path` stays
separate from that artifact path in structured diagnostics. A file
export failure does not undo an already saved handoff. Reconcile its returned
operation result before repeating the save; never treat it as a reason to repeat
remote generation.
